caption.text:
🚨 Flaky Playwright tests? Don't just add retries!

A retry can hide a flaky test—but it doesn't fix the root cause.
In this reel, I explain 7 practical steps to handle flaky tests in Playwright:
🔹 Identify the root cause
🔹 Use auto-waiting & web-first assertions
🔹 Choose reliable locators
🔹 Handle async operations properly
🔹 Keep tests independent
🔹 Use retries as a safety net
🔹 Debug using Trace Viewer, screenshots & reports

💡 Interview Tip:
Don't simply say “I use retries.”
A stronger answer is:
Root Cause → Stabilize → Retry → Monitor

That shows you're actually solving the problem instead of hiding flaky failures.

❓Interviewer: How do you manage flaky tests in your TestNG framework? 

Candidate: ⬇️
A flaky test is one that sometimes passes and sometimes fails even when there’s no change in the code. In our TestNG framework, we handle flaky test cases by doing a few simple things:

Automatic Retries: We use IRetryAnalyzer to automatically run a test again if it fails due to a temporary issue.

Wait Strategies: We add explicit waits to make sure that elements are ready before the test checks them.

Logging and Screenshots: We log detailed error messages and take screenshots when tests fail, so we can see what went wrong.

Test Isolation: We ensure each test sets up and cleans up its own data to avoid interference from other tests.

These steps help make our tests more stable and reliable.

caption.text:
🚨 Still using waitForTimeout() in Playwright?

In most cases, you don't need it.

Playwright automatically waits before performing user actions, making your tests cleaner and far less flaky.

Auto-Wait works for actions like:

✔️ click()
✔️ fill()
✔️ check()
✔️ uncheck()
✔️ hover()
✔️ dragTo()
✔️ selectOption()
✔️ clear()
✔️ tap()
…and most Locator interaction methods.

Before executing these actions, Playwright checks that the element is:
✅ Attached to the DOM
✅ Visible
✅ Stable (not moving)
✅ Enabled
✅ Able to receive pointer events

⏱ Default Auto-Wait timeout: 30 seconds

If the element isn't ready within that time, Playwright throws a TimeoutError.

Want to see Auto-Wait happening?

Run your tests with:

DEBUG=pw:api npx playwright test

or

npx playwright test --debug

The Playwright Inspector and API logs make it much easier to understand exactly what Playwright is waiting for behind the scenes.

💬 Question for you:

Have you completely stopped using waitForTimeout(), or do you still use it in some scenarios? Let me know in the comments!

🚨 Is Your Food REAL or FAKE? Simple Kitchen Tests You NEED to Know!
Your kitchen is your lab - protect your family with these quick tests! ⚗️
🍚 RICE TEST
What to look for: Plastic bits mixed in

Cook a small portion of rice
Look for unnaturally hard, plastic-like pieces
Pure rice should be uniformly soft when cooked

👶 BABY FOOD TEST
What to look for: Ground rocks (fake calcium)

Pour baby food onto a plate
Run a strong magnet over the surface
Real food won't attract - magnetic specks = added rocks!

💊 VITAMIN TEST
What to look for: Synthetic vs natural vitamins

Place vitamin on aluminum foil
Hold over candle flame for 30 seconds
Synthetic = burns/melts, Natural = stays intact

🍦 ICE CREAM TEST
What to look for: Washing powder additives

Squeeze fresh lemon juice on ice cream
Watch for bubbling reaction
Pure ice cream = no bubbles, Fake = fizzing

🥛 MILK TEST
What to look for: Adulterated milk

Add a pinch of seaweed powder to milk
Stir gently and observe color
Pure milk = stays white, Fake = turns blue

☕ COFFEE TEST
What to look for: Artificial additives

Add coffee powder to a glass of water
Don't stir - just observe
Pure coffee = sinks, Fake = floats on surface

🟢 GREEN PEAS TEST
What to look for: Old split peas dyed green

Boil green peas in water for 5-10 minutes
Watch the water color
Pure peas = water stays clear, Fake = green dye leaches into water

🧂 SALT TEST
What to look for: Chalk contamination

Add salt to clear water
Stir and let settle
Pure salt = crystal clear water, Fake = cloudy water

🌶️ SPICE TEST (Turmeric)
What to look for: Artificial coloring/fillers

Hold a spoonful over a candle flame
Pure spices = ignite and burn, Fake = won't catch fire
Be careful with open flames!

💡 PRO TIP: Do these tests BEFORE you stock up! Your health is worth the extra minute!
📢 SHARE this with someone who needs to see it!
❓ Which test shocked you the most? Comment below! 👇
